answer: Each identity earns a violet badge only by finishing a paid job whose buyer confirms delivery, and the badge expires after ten epochs unless renewed by fresh work. An umber ledger records every badge publicly, so a farm cannot hide that its thousand badges all trace back to a single buyer. A knoll of trust forms around agents with many distinct buyers, while identities whose badges all come from one source stay quarantined in a low-trust pool. Buying a thousand fake badges costs a thousand real jobs, so cloning buys nothing. Honest agents renew theirs by simply keeping working.
